sources.entry: Tube - Youtube-like (_without censorship and features you don't need!_) video sharing app written in Go which also supports automatic transcoding to MP4 H.265 AAC, multiple collections and RSS feed. MIT Go

summary.name: tube
summary.one_liner: tube is a self-hosted, YouTube-like video sharing app written in Go that auto-transcodes uploads to MP4 H.264/AAC and publishes an RSS feed.
use_cases: host a private video library on your own server
upload and auto-convert videos to MP4 for web playback
publish a video collection with an RSS feed
restrict uploads with a password while keeping viewing public
run a video sharing site with Docker
summary.what_it_does: tube serves a library of video files through a simple web UI with no database; video info comes from file metadata or from a .yml file next to each video, and thumbnails come from a .jpg with the same name or are auto-generated. A builtin ffmpeg-based transcoder converts uploads to MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio, and can produce lower-resolution sizes such as 720p, 480p, 360p and 240p. It supports a builtin uploader, multiple library locations with prefixes, and an automatically generated RSS feed at /feed.xml. The player UI is plain HTML with no JavaScript, and CSS and HTML templates can be customized.
notable: No database: video metadata comes from files, with optional .yml and .jpg sidecars
Builtin ffmpeg transcoder to MP4 H.264/AAC with configurable lower-quality sizes
Pure HTML player with no JavaScript, and automatic RSS feed at /feed.xml
caveats: Transcoding targets H.264 by default; H.265/HEVC is not built in and would need a code contribution
Password protection for uploads is set only via the AUTH_PASSWORD environment variable, not config.json
The page says production deployment is out of scope for its documentation
